Ui.Script:
-- ── _ERRORMESSAGE / message (ref BasicControls.xml l.5-15) ───────────────────────────── -- -- VERBATIM, including `debuginfo()`. That line was guarded here when this file landed, -- because `debuginfo` was an engine global we lacked and whose behaviour was uncarved — -- and declaring a no-op under a real 1.12 name is exactly the "capability absent without a -- failure" class 1203 named. wow-re has since carved it (2026-08-11): `0x7027f0` is -- `33 c0 c3` — `xor eax,eax; ret`, three bytes, no call, no memory write. It genuinely -- does nothing and returns nothing, and five of its `debug*` siblings are byte-identical. -- So the no-op in `stdlib.rs` is the REFERENCE's no-op, the guard was measuring our own -- ignorance rather than a real branch, and it is gone. function _ERRORMESSAGE(msg) debuginfo() if not ScriptErrors:IsVisible() then ScriptErrors_Message:SetText(msg) ScriptErrors:Show() end return msg end
function message(text) _ERRORMESSAGE(text) end
-- ── AND ONE LINE OF THE REFERENCE DELIBERATELY NOT TRANSCRIBED ───────────────────────── -- The reference ends this block with `seterrorhandler(_ERRORMESSAGE);`. We do not. -- -- benilla's default handler is `__benilla_script_error` (decision 1195), which pushes into -- `UiScript::errors()` — the channel the corpus harness's whole blocker table is built on, -- and the only place a Lua fault is visible to any instrument we own. Installing -- `_ERRORMESSAGE` would route every runtime error into a modal dialog instead and blind -- `blockers`, `demand` and every A/B that depends on them, to buy a dialog nobody has asked -- for yet. -- -- The addon-facing behaviour is unchanged either way: `geterrorhandler()` still answers a -- callable (the 1195 pair), `geterrorhandler()(msg)` still reports, and an addon that -- installs its OWN handler with `seterrorhandler` still wins outright. What differs is only -- which handler is installed when nobody has chosen — and that is ours to choose while the -- error channel is load-bearing for the arc's instruments. Revisit when a player-facing -- Lua-error surface exists; the one line is the whole change.
-- ── TEXT (ref l.22-26, verbatim) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- "This function is used to translate text (actually it's already translated as-is)" is -- the reference's own comment. It really is the identity function: 1.12 shipped one -- localisation per client and the hook was never used. function TEXT(text) return text end
-- ── UIParentLoadAddOn (ref UIParent.lua l.638-647) ──────────────────────────────────── -- The on-demand loader every "open the auction house / tradeskill / talent panel" path -- goes through, and the one 5 corpus addons name — FuBar_MCPFu, Fubar_RareTrackerFu, MCP, -- MikScrollingBattleText, SpecialTalent: five separate addons, not one library replicated -- (1207/1240). -- -- Every piece was already here and only the join was missing: `LoadAddOn` answers the -- reference's own `(1, nil)` / `(nil, reason)` pair, `message` and `TEXT` are directly -- above, and the `ADDON_*` reason words come from the real `GlobalStrings.lua` we RUN off -- the patch chain rather than copy (1234). -- -- **`FailedAddOnLoad` is the reference's own latch, and it is not decoration.** Without it -- an addon that retries the load from a handler raises a modal on every attempt; with it -- the failure shows once per addon name per session. It is exactly the detail this would -- have lacked had it been reconstructed from the name instead of read. -- -- Every reason our `LoadAddOn` can answer resolves to a string: MISSING, DISABLED, -- NOT_DEMAND_LOADED, DEP_MISSING and DEP_DISABLED all have an `ADDON_..reason` word -- (GlobalStrings l.16-31), the same reason set wow-re's `ui.md` l.2396 carves off -- `0x51e780`. So the `getglobal` below cannot hand `format` a nil. FailedAddOnLoad = {};
function UIParentLoadAddOn(name) local loaded, reason = LoadAddOn(name) if not loaded then if not FailedAddOnLoad[name] then message(format(TEXT(ADDON_LOAD_FAILED), name, TEXT(getglobal("ADDON_" .. reason)))) FailedAddOnLoad[name] = true end end return loaded end
